name: Pascal Sirguey
description: Named contributor in sourced geospatial conference and publication records.
story: GeoCart 2014 accepted abstracts, New Zealand Cartographic Society lists Pascal Sirguey as an author of “Geographical vector agents for supervised image classification”; “A multi-epoch triangulation of stereo ASTER images for Tasman Glacier elevation change”.

GeoCart 2016 conference programme, New Zealand Cartographic Society lists Pascal Sirguey as an author of “Underground laser scanning and the LiDARRAS project”; “Photogrammetric modelling in RPAS aerial surveys”; “Seasonal snowpack mapping with drone photogrammetry”.

Cartographies of change: GeoCart 2018 proceedings, National Library of New Zealand record 40158196 lists Pascal Sirguey as an author of “Snow depth distribution from high-resolution RPAS photogrammetry”; “High-resolution tussock distribution modelling in the Pisa Range”; “RPAS topographic surveys”.

GeoCart session 1 programme, New Zealand Cartographic Society (archived programme page) lists Pascal Sirguey as an author of “Banks Peninsula subtidal habitat mapping”; “Southern Alps snow resources from satellite photogrammetry”.
GeoCart 2024 session 2 programme, New Zealand Cartographic Society lists Pascal Sirguey as an author of “Watching the Wetlands”.
GeoCart 2024 session 3 programme, New Zealand Cartographic Society lists Pascal Sirguey as an author of “Digital Geomorphology: Repeat UAV Lidar Mapping of Aoraki/Mount Cook’s Changing Landscape”.

Aubrey Miller staff profile: NZGRC 2022 Matariki Project proceedings citation, University of Otago lists Pascal Sirguey as an author of “The Matariki Project: 3-D change detection with satellite photogrammetric mapping”.

SIRC NZ 2013 GIS and remote sensing proceedings citations, University of Otago lists Pascal Sirguey as an author of “Snowfall detection in Antarctica using MODIS infrared reflectance”; “Modelling ice retreat on Kilimanjaro using GIS”; “Recent ice wastage on the Tasman Glacier from geodetic elevation changes”; “Geographical vector agent modelling for image classification”.
